2. A FIRST MISMATCH MEANS STILL SYNCING: retry, with progress persisted OUTSIDE the lake.
3. PAST THE MANIFEST'S OWN deadline_at IT IS A FAILED DELIVERY, raised with evidence: which file, expected vs observed size, expected vs observed digest. For a legacy mtime-based manifest FREEZE the deadline on first observation -- consumer-side mtime can reset on sync.
4. A RECEIPT ON DISK IS A CACHE whose identity must match the manifest digest, never an authority.
5. IDEMPOTENCE on (store_id, snapshot_id, table_name): same snapshot is a NO-OP; a new snapshot_seq writes a new immutable version. This replaces _lookup_existing_genome_id's skipped_already_ingested behaviour, under which a reload is a silent no-op EVEN WHEN THE GENOME HAS CHANGED.

THE HASHES, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES -- do not conflate them and do not create any column named assembly_hash:
  assembly_entity_hash = standardizers.entity_hash('genome', contigs) -- each contig canonicalized by the DNA rule, EMPTY contigs DROPPED, the remainder SORTED, '|'-joined, sha256 of the UTF-8 bytes. ORDER-INDEPENDENT. This is the OUTWARD clearinghouse identity and joins to clearinghouse.genome_entity.
  assembly_content_hash = KBDL genomes.content_hash -- sha256 over canonical FASTA bytes, header-inclusive, ORDER-DEPENDENT. Identifies THIS representation. Equate it with fasta_object_id ONLY where the pinned object-format contract proves that equality; if a storage id hashes COMPRESSED bytes, the equality is false.
Measured, so you can check yourself against it: live fitness.assembly_hash follows rule A (verified by recomputing both rules over three real assemblies of 1, 16 and 7 contigs from KBase workspace 262939 -- A matched all three, B none).

genome: genome_id (KBDL's G-number) is the logical key; assembly_entity_hash is a MANY-to-one FK. Two biologically distinct genomes CAN share one assembly -- live fitness has exactly that (SyringaeB728a and SyringaeB728a_mexBdelta, a wild-type and its knockout mutant, byte-identical assemblies, 48 genomes over 47 distinct hashes). A loader keying genome on the hash would MERGE a mutant into its parent. Taxonomy is TaxonomyBlock's EIGHT fields flattened -- genus, species, lineage, ncbi_taxid, ani, reference, reason, source_database -- all of them, because a taxonomy call that cannot say why it was made is not reusable.

genome_alias: APPEND-ONLY, MULTI-VALUED, NO UNIQUENESS, FILL-ONLY. Emit from the KBDL genomes row, whose schema is (genome_id, owner, content_hash, prefix, fasta_object_id, genome_object_id, skani_hits_json, taxonomy_json, created_at, created_by_job_id): kbdl_genome_id from genome_id, kbdl_object_id from genome_object_id, kbdl_fasta_object_id from fasta_object_id, plus assembly_accession, arc_subject and ncbi_taxid where known. MEASURED CAVEAT you must handle rather than assume away: 0 of 4,865 genomes have a genome_object_id or fasta_object_id appearing as an old_object_id, and there are 0 chains of depth > 1 -- so this path has NO live coverage and your fixtures are its only test. CALL THE VALIDATORS on every row, and the ZERO-JOIN GUARD before every relationship assertion.

parallel_group.prompt:
GENE IDENTITY IS SCOPED BY AN ANNOTATION RUN -- READ THIS FIRST, IT CHANGES THE KEY. Populate genome_build (one row per BUILD) and carry build_id on gene, gene_qualifier, genome_build_provenance and genome_caller_run. gene is keyed on (build_id, gene_id), NOT gene_id alone.

WHY: genome_id is derived from the assembly CONTENT HASH and does NOT change when the caller changes, and genome_registry._lookup_existing_genome_id DEDUPES ON content_hash -- a HIT returns the EXISTING genome_id. So rebuilding one assembly with gene_caller='bakta' after an 'inprocess' build yields the SAME genome_id, the SAME {genome_id}_{N} id space, and DIFFERENT coordinates. Keying on gene_id alone is a silent collision. The measured analogue: Siqueira et al. 2025 (doi:10.1101/2025.05.27.656432) compared the GenBank and RefSeq annotations of ONE IDENTICAL P. putida KT2440 assembly and found 897 genes -- ~16% of ORFs -- with IDENTICAL locus tags at DIFFERENT genomic positions. Every schema that faces this keeps the sets apart (INSDC GCA vs GCF, Ensembl's parallel otherfeatures database, Chado's analysisfeature unique (feature_id, analysis_id)). Do NOT merge competing callers onto one row.

build_id IS FULLY SPECIFIED -- a hash with no byte serialization is not a key:
  build_id = sha256(canonical_json({'identity_version': 1, 'genome_id': <str>, 'assembly_content_hash': <str>, 'structural_features_digest': <str>, 'caller_identity': {'gene_caller': <str|null>, 'callers': {<pkg>: <ver|null>}, 'bakta_db': <str|null>, 'bakta_image': <str|null>, 'bakta_driver_sha256': <str|null>, 'cds_overlap_drop_fraction': <canonical decimal string|null>}}))
canonical_json is RFC-8785-style: SORTED object keys, no insignificant whitespace, EXPLICIT NULLS (never omitted keys), UTF-8. Floating thresholds are encoded as CANONICAL DECIMAL STRINGS, never floats, so 0.5 and 0.50 cannot mint two build ids for one build. structural_features_digest covers EVERY CDS and non-coding feature and its qualifiers in FEATURE-ID ORDER and EXCLUDES taxonomy and all downstream annotation results -- so a non-coding enrichment DOES change the build id (which a metadata-only tuple would not) while a re-annotation does not. PUBLISH GOLDEN INPUT/PREIMAGE/DIGEST VECTORS as a deliverable: a hash rule with no test vectors cannot be reimplemented.
ALSO CARRY coordinate_convention ('span'|'kbase_location') AS A BUILD FIELD. KBDL's CoordinateConvention is genuinely ambiguous at the source and is resolved per-build by the adapter (or required when no DNA is present to disambiguate). A strand or coordinate mistake hashes the WRONG DNA while producing entirely plausible rows, so derive DNA via the pinned canonical coordinate/strand extraction routine and publish test vectors for BOTH STRANDS and for boundary intervals.
THERE IS NO MUTABLE COLUMN. genome_build.source_designated_current records what the SOURCE said and is immutable. Build currency is an APPEND-ONLY DECLARATION in genome_build_currency, projected by 'greatest declared_at per genome_id with a deterministic declaration_id tie-break, falling back to source_designated_current'. Do NOT write a mutable flag and do NOT have the loader pick a winner by overwriting.

Extend the genome_companion loader in KBUtilLib to the FEATURE and PROVENANCE tables: gene, gene_qualifier, genome_build_provenance, genome_caller_run.

SOURCE SHAPES, read from kbdl_service.schemas.build_genome -- do not guess them:
  CanonicalGenome = genome_id, prefix, taxonomy, contigs, features, non_coding_features, non_coding_provenance
  CanonicalFeature = id, source_id (str|None), location, dna_sequence, protein_translation (REQUIRED, non-empty)
  CanonicalNonCodingFeature = id, source_id (str|None), type, location, dna_sequence, product, partial, caller, amino_acid, anticodon, ncrna_class, rfam -- with model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow') and NO protein_translation field at all (the key is rejected outright)
  NonCodingType = tRNA, rRNA, tmRNA, ncRNA, misc_RNA, repeat_region -- SIX members. repeat_region is a CRISPR array and is NOT an RNA gene.
  NonCodingProvenance = source ('called'|'source'|'none'), callers (dict package->version, INCLUDING CALLERS THAT RAN AND FOUND NOTHING), cds_dropped_overlapping_rna, cds_overlap_drop_fraction (None = 'not recorded' = built under the original any-overlap rule), gene_caller ('bakta'|'inprocess'|None, where None means an ANNOTATED source whose genes were called by someone else years ago), cds_discarded (dict reason->count, the CALLER's vocabulary not ours), bakta_db (a string like '6.0-full', deliberately NOT an ObjectRef -- what reproduces a call is which database CONTENT was used), bakta_image, bakta_driver_sha256.

gene -- one row per feature, coding and non-coding in ONE table.
  gene_id is the KBDL feature id VERBATIM. KBDL mints f'{genome_id}_{N}' for CDS and f'{genome_id}_nc{N}' for non-coding, on INDEPENDENT counters (genome_normalize.py, two sites). So '{g}_1' and '{g}_nc1' coexist and cannot collide. Carry them unchanged -- an id in the lake must be pasteable into KBDL with no translation table to go stale. A dropped feature consumes no id number, so the counters are not dense and you must not assume they are.
  feature_type = 'CDS' for every CanonicalFeature, and the NonCodingType value for every CanonicalNonCodingFeature.
  protein_seq_hash set ONLY for CDS; dna_seq_hash ALWAYS set. The validators enforce the iff in both directions -- call them.
  locus_id = source_id, NULL for an ab initio call (there is no upstream identifier to record).
  caller/caller_version: KBDL records a single string, either the literal 'source' for a feature carried through from an annotated input, or '<package> <version>' for an ab initio call (e.g. 'pyaragorn 0.3.0'). SPLIT IT into caller and caller_version. 'source' has no version; decide and DOCUMENT what caller_version is in that case, and make the choice consistent with the validator's mandatory-version rule rather than fighting it.
  product, partial, amino_acid, anticodon, ncrna_class, rfam from the non-coding model; rpt_family from the extra keys, carrying 'CRISPR' for a repeat_region.
  OVERLAPPING COORDINATES MUST BE LEGAL. kbdl-add-non-coding-to-existing-genome-v1 deliberately does NOT drop a CDS that overlaps an added RNA, so existing CDS ids stay valid -- which means gene rows for one genome CAN overlap. Any uniqueness or validation must PERMIT it. v2_genes effectively never had this case.

gene_qualifier -- the narrow sidecar for the extra='allow' passthrough. EXACTLY ONE ROW PER UNPROMOTED EXTRA KEY, and value holds CANONICAL JSON for EVERY type -- strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects and explicit null -- preserving array order and duplicates. str(value) cannot distinguish a source string from serialized structure, cannot round-trip an array, and unrolling a list would invent an order and duplicate policy. Keys PROMOTED to named columns on gene (product, partial, amino_acid, anticodon, ncrna_class, rfam, rpt_family) are EXCLUDED from this table so nothing appears twice. Qualifier frequency counts DISTINCT (build_id, gene_id) occurrences per qualifier key. Carry them rather than dropping them: an annotated GenBank source can hold qualifiers nobody enumerated, and the dropped keys would by definition be the ones nobody thought to test for. ALSO count rows per distinct qualifier into the load ledger, so that promoting a frequent qualifier to a named column later is an evidenced decision rather than a guess.

genome_build_provenance -- one row per genome, from NonCodingProvenance's nine fields. cds_discarded goes to cds_discarded_json as CANONICAL JSON (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) because its keys are the caller's vocabulary and would otherwise force a schema change every time Bakta adds a discard reason. Preserve the MEANING OF NULL on cds_overlap_drop_fraction -- it is 'not recorded', i.e. built under the original rule where any overlap of >=1bp dropped the CDS, and it must not be defaulted to a number. Likewise gene_caller NULL means an annotated source and must not be defaulted to 'inprocess'.

genome_caller_run -- ONE ROW PER CALLER THAT RAN, INCLUDING ZERO-HIT RUNS. features_called MEANS RETAINED CANONICAL NON-CODING FEATURES ATTRIBUTED TO THAT PACKAGE -- NOT raw pre-filter caller hits. The distinction is the whole point: counting survivors as if they were raw hits would label a caller zero-hit when filtering or deduplication removed everything it found, which is a DIFFERENT fact and the opposite of what this table is for. If raw hit counts are wanted as science, the PRODUCER must deliver them as their own field; do not infer them. A MISSING HISTORICAL VERSION STAYS NULL WITH A RECORDED QUALITY DIAGNOSTIC -- never a guessed default, because inventing provenance is worse than admitting its absence. Unroll NonCodingProvenance.callers (package -> version) into rows and set features_called from the actual count of features attributed to that caller, WHICH MAY BE 0. THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE TABLE: 'zero tRNAs' and 'the tRNA caller never ran' are different facts about a genome, and without the zero-hit row they are indistinguishable -- a later rebuild could not tell a genuinely tRNA-free assembly from one built before tRNA calling existed. ABSENCE of a row means the caller did not run; features_called = 0 means it ran and found nothing. Never infer the first from a missing count.
  NOTE a shape that is real and not a contradiction: a bare-FASTA genome built with call_non_coding=False has non_coding_source='none' AND a gene_caller that certainly ran. So source='none' with a non-null gene_caller is valid input, not corrupt input.

WRITE TESTS that assert, at minimum:
  - a genome whose caller ran and found nothing produces a genome_caller_run row with features_called = 0; AND a genome where that caller never ran produces NO row for it. BOTH assertions must be present -- testing only the first cannot distinguish the two states, which is the entire reason the table exists.
  - a CanonicalNonCodingFeature loads with protein_seq_hash NULL and its type in feature_type, and a repeat_region loads with rpt_family = 'CRISPR'.
  - a CDS overlapping an RNA gene in the same genome loads BOTH rows and rejects neither.
  - an extra='allow' qualifier that has no named column lands in gene_qualifier rather than being dropped.
  - cds_overlap_drop_fraction=None round-trips as NULL and is not defaulted; gene_caller=None round-trips as NULL.
  - a non-dense id sequence (a dropped feature consumed no number) loads without the loader assuming density.
  - '{g}_1' and '{g}_nc1' in the same genome are two distinct rows.
  - THE REBUILD CASE: load one genome built 'inprocess', then THE SAME genome rebuilt with gene_caller='bakta' at DIFFERENT coordinates. Assert TWO genome_build rows, BOTH full gene sets retained, ONE genome/assembly/contig set (not duplicated), exactly ONE genome_build_currency declaration projecting as current, that a gene_id-only query WITHOUT build_id returns TWO rows (the collision the key prevents -- make it visible, do not hide it), and that published_current_gene returns ONE.
  - BUILD_ID GOLDEN VECTORS: a reordered callers dict yields the SAME digest; 0.5 and 0.50 yield the SAME digest; an explicit null is distinguished from a missing key; a non-coding ENRICHMENT yields a DIFFERENT digest while a re-annotation yields the SAME one.
  - QUALIFIER ROUND-TRIP, mixed types: string, integer, float, boolean, explicit null, array with duplicates and preserved order, nested object -- all round-trip through gene_qualifier.value as canonical JSON; and a PROMOTED key (rpt_family) appears on gene and NOT in the sidecar.
  - features_called COUNTS RETAINED FEATURES: a fixture where the caller emits features that are then filtered out asserts the retained count, not the raw count.

THE FOREIGN KEY IS (build_id, gene_id), NEVER gene_id ALONE. gene is keyed on (build_id, gene_id) per Q4, so every annotation and fitness row must carry the build_id of the structural call it annotates. Extend the genome_companion loader in KBUtilLib to the ANNOTATION and FITNESS tables: function, function_annotation, ontology_term, ontology_annotation, transyt_annotation, condition, essentiality, experimental_fitness, propagated_fitness.

THE NARROW SHAPE IS THE DECISION, and it is the shape the live fitness namespace already uses for these three tables -- one row per (gene, assignment, tool), with the TOOL AS A COLUMN. Do not build a wide tool-shaped table. The live wide table, fitness.annotation, has rast/ko/bakta as COLUMNS, does not generalise to the six-tool set, AND is 100% orphaned (all 272,076 rows fail to join gene.gene_id, because its feature_id is 'organism:locus' while gene_id is '{uuid}.{locus}', over 60 organisms against gene's 48 genomes). It is not carried forward. Adding a seventh tool must be a load, not a migration.

THREE CHANGES FROM THE LIVE SHAPE, each deliberate:

1. NO evidence TABLE AND NO evidence_id. The live fitness.evidence is a strict 1:1 satellite carrying no information: 2,504,043 rows = function_annotation 1,118,422 + ontology_annotation 1,010,656 + transyt_annotation 374,965 exactly, and the per-tool split reconciles for all six tools; it has 0 non-null evidence_score and 0 non-null evidence_probability; its evidence_type merely repeats the parent row's tool; and it holds only 2,388,346 distinct evidence_id values so it is not even a key. Its one potentially-useful field becomes a nullable `score DOUBLE` column ON the annotation row. Do not recreate the indirection.

2. tool_version IS MANDATORY AND MUST BE POPULATED. The live source_version column is NULL in 100% of rows -- 0 of 1,118,422 on function_annotation and 0 of 1,010,656 on ontology_annotation. The validators from P4 require it; satisfy them with the real tool version from the KBDLGenomeAnnotation result rather than by weakening the validator. If the delivered bundle genuinely does not carry a tool version for some annotation, that is a defect in the PRODUCER side and must be reported as such -- do NOT write a placeholder string, and do NOT relax the rule.

3. ONE PINNED SOURCE-TO-TARGET MAPPING AND ONE FIXTURE PER TOOL IS A DELIVERABLE OF THIS TASK. Tool outputs are NOT interchangeable schemas: nothing in the destination columns says which number is score, which text defines a function_id, or how a version and parameter set are extracted, and the six tools (BAKTA, PROKKA, DRAM2, RAST, KOFAMSCAN, TRANSYT) differ in all three. Ship the mapping and the fixture, do not infer.

A record whose required tool_version or parameter set cannot be recovered is QUARANTINED with a recorded diagnostic -- never given a placeholder. A quarantined REQUIRED field makes the batch UNPUBLISHABLE, so a legacy record cannot silently become a published result, but one bad record does not fail a whole corpus either. Make that choice explicit in code, not implicit.
5. RESOLVE THE BUILD FROM THE ANNOTATION JOB'S ACTUAL INPUT GENOME OBJECT, NEVER FROM WHICHEVER BUILD IS CURRENTLY DESIGNATED CURRENT. Resolving through a currency projection retroactively re-attributes historical evidence when currency changes. An annotation whose input build cannot be recovered is quarantined, not attached to a guess.
6. parameter_set_hash IS CARRIED AND RESOLVES OUTWARD. It is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the parameter set the tool ran under -- see kbutillib.domains.identity.parameter_set_hash; a default run is {} whose hash is DEFAULT_PARAMETER_SET_HASH. It resolves against the EXISTING kbaseincubator.clearinghouse.parameter_set registry, which already keeps the pre-image (canonical_json) so the hash rule stays recomputable. DO NOT MINT A SECOND REGISTRY. Honour the registry's writer obligation: append any registry row BEFORE the annotation rows that reference it, so that an orphan check -- distinct parameter_set_hash values in the annotation tables absent from the registry -- comes back empty. Add that orphan check as an assertion the loader runs.

TOOL VOCABULARY, measured live: function_annotation carries BAKTA, DRAM2, PROKKA, RAST; ontology_annotation carries BAKTA, DRAM2, PROKKA, KOFAMSCAN; transyt_annotation is TRANSYT's own table with a tool-specific payload (reaction_equation, tc_number, substrate) and is kept as its own table because that payload is genuinely tool-shaped. Ontology namespaces measured live: KO 8,685, GO 4,468, COG 3,992, EC 3,617.

THE FITNESS LAYER (condition, essentiality, experimental_fitness, propagated_fitness) is carried from the live scheme UNCHANGED in shape plus the provenance tail -- it is the part of fitness that works. Two notes: the live `group` column on condition is renamed condition_group in the schema module because `group` is a reserved word, so MAP IT; and propagated_fitness is the volume table (14,076,257 rows live, and it grows with genomes x conditions), so it is the one most exposed to the sharded-writer work in the next phase.

EVERY ONE OF THOSE PASSES VACUOUSLY OVER AN EMPTY TABLE, which is why the guard runs first.
